text:
alex chen: Heads-up — product wants a concise dashboard showing KV + prefix cache effectiveness. Key asks: hit rate, eviction counts, and reuse patterns by workload. Who should own what for instrumentation vs rollups?

maya patel: My vote: runtime emits low-level counters + minimal tags; telemetry/infra owns rollups, derived metrics, and the Grafana dashboards. Runtime should avoid exploding cardinality.

samir kohli: Agree. We need a small spec: metric names, allowed label sets, and recommended cardinality caps. Then runtime PR + telemetry ingestion mapping.

rachel ng: Can we enumerate required metrics? Also call out what must NOT be emitted (e.g., per-prompt hashes).

alex chen: Initial spec idea: 
- redwood_cache_hits_total{cache="kv|prefix", model, route, tenant?}
- redwood_cache_misses_total{cache, model, route, tenant?}
- redwood_cache_evictions_total{cache, reason="size|ttl|policy|reallocate", model?, route?}
- redwood_prefix_reuse_buckets{model, route, reuse_bucket="0|1|2-5|6-20|21+"}
- redwood_prefix_length_avg{model, route} (gauge)
We derive hit rate from hits/(hits+misses) in telemetry.

evan li: For reuse we should use a histogram-like bucket approach but with a stable label for bucket. That keeps series count bounded. Also a heatmap panel that shows reuse density across top N workloads.

maya patel: We should emit eviction events as a low-cardinality OTLP span when eviction happens, with fields: reason, bucketed_prefix_length, ttl_bucket, and maybe a small sample_id. No free-text or per-prefix values.

samir kohli: Implementation constraints: runtime must limit labels to (model, route, tenant_flag) by default. For hosted plan, tenant label is omitted to reduce cardinality; enterprise clusters can opt in. We'll document cardinality guidance in the PR.

ops-bot: metric stub created: redwood_cache_hits_total

rachel ng: Dashboard sketch: 
Top row: global hit rates (kv vs prefix) + change vs 24h. 
Second row: model-level hit rates with sparklines. 
Third row: reuse heatmap (time x reuse_bucket) for top 20 routes. 
Fourth row: eviction reasons (pie) + eviction rate timeseries + table of top evicting routes (aggregated, sortable).

alex chen: Alerts: primary alert if derived hit_rate drops below 70% for 5m. Secondary alert for eviction spikes (>5x baseline) or sudden drop in reuse (>50% vs baseline). Rachel/SRE can tune thresholds.

maya patel: Telemetry pipeline plan: ingest OTLP counters, emit 1m/5m rollups, compute derived gauge redwood_cache_hit_rate{cache,model,route}. Also maintain per-model aggregated series and a global fallback. Downsampled raw counters retained for 7d, rollups for 30d.

evan li: Grafana TODOs: folder + JSON panels. I'll stub panels with mocked queries and dummy data. Panels: heatmap (reuse_bucket), stacked series (hits/misses), table (top routes), and alert rules (Prometheus/Grafana Alerting).

samir kohli: Runtime TODOs: add Prom counters and an OTLP eviction event. Code sketch: 
```ncacheHits.WithLabelValues("prefix", model, route).Inc()
cacheMisses.WithLabelValues("prefix", model, route).Inc()
evictions.WithLabelValues("kv", "ttl", model).Inc()
```
I'll include label guidance and a feature flag for tenant label emission.

rachel ng: SRE notes: anomaly detection on reuse patterns is useful. We should add a job that compares sliding windows and fires an incident when change is significant. Also add runbook pointers in the dashboard.

alex chen: Ownership: I will draft an RFC with checklist and link to Grafana folder. @maya will own telemetry schema, @evan will create dashboard JSON, @samir will PR runtime counters, @rachel will write alert rules + runbook.

maya patel: I'll put a telemetry schema doc in the infra repo and include example PromQL/Flux queries and rollup rules.

evan li: I'll create a Grafana folder with a mocked dataset and attach the JSON panels.

samir kohli: I'll open the runtime PR and include a note about not emitting prompt-level labels.

rachel ng: I'll draft alert definitions and include example runbook steps: how to check top evicting routes, how to check model-level reuse, and when to escalate to ML team.

alex chen: Meeting to align on cardinality and RBAC: Thursday 10:00. I'll create the RFC issue after the meeting and include a checklist for telemetry rollout.

maya patel: Invite sent. :calendar:

ops-bot: calendar event created: "KV/Prefix cache metrics sync" Thu 10:00 by maya.patel

alex chen: Thanks all — target: telemetry schema landed by next Tue so dashboards can be mocked mid-week.
